normalized_address_fields.name: normalized_address_fields
normalized_address_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS person_id,
  NULL AS address_row_id,
  NULL AS full_name,
  NULL AS address_purpose,

  -- room: canonicalize BUILDING_ROOM: trim, empty -> NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(`BUILDING_ROOM`), '') AS room,

  -- floor: canonicalize FLOOR: trim, empty -> NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(`FLOOR`), '') AS floor,

  -- building_key: use SPACE_UNIT_CODE as-is but trim and NULL-normalize
  NULLIF(TRIM(`SPACE_UNIT_CODE`), '') AS building_key,

  -- building_street_address: construct from BUILDING_COMPONENT (trim/NULL)
  NULLIF(TRIM(`BUILDING_COMPONENT`), '') AS building_street_address,

  -- building_city: not present in source table, expose as NULL (can't derive)
  NULL AS building_city,

  -- building_state: not present in source table, expose as NULL (can't derive)
  NULL AS building_state,

  -- building_postal_code: not present in source table, expose as NULL (can't derive)
  NULL AS building_postal_code
FROM `zpm_rooms_load`
normalized_address_fields.description: Canonicalize and project the address and building fields (trim/NULL-normalize/standardize columns) so room, floor, building key, and building address parts are in consistent form.

person_office_candidates.name: person_office_candidates
person_office_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  NORM.person_id                                AS person_id,
  NORM.address_row_id                            AS address_row_id,
  NORM.room                                      AS room,
  NORM.floor                                     AS floor,
  NORM.building_key                              AS building_key,
  NORM.building_street_address                   AS building_street_address,
  NORM.building_city                              AS building_city,
  NORM.building_state                             AS building_state,
  NORM.building_postal_code                       AS building_postal_code,
  NORM.full_name                                  AS full_name,
  NORM.address_purpose                            AS address_purpose
FROM normalized_address_fields AS NORM
WHERE
  -- Person filter: keep only rows that belong to the target person.
  -- Lift any person-specific literal out of the view; the caller should supply the person_id filter.
  1 = 1
  -- Address purpose filter: keep only street/office address purposes.
  -- Lift any purpose-specific literal out of the view; the caller should supply the purpose filter.
  AND 1 = 1
person_office_candidates.description: Filter the normalized address rows to those that belong to the target person and have the address purpose indicating a street/office address (apply the person name and purpose filters).
counter_examples: What is the room, floor, building key, building street address, city, state, and postal code of Professor Summer Haynes's office?
Among the mailing lists subscribed by people with physical offices in building 24, provide the name of the most subscribed mailing list and the total number of subscribers.

subject_category_year_enroll_fee.name: subject_category_year_enroll_fee
subject_category_year_enroll_fee.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS subject_id,
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS iap_category_id,
  c.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS iap_category_name,
  s.TERM_CODE AS academic_year,
  s.FEE AS fee_amount,
  s.MAX_ENROLLMENT AS enrollment_count
FROM iap_subject_detail AS s
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_category AS c
  ON s.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = c.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
subject_category_year_enroll_fee.description: Join the basic IAP subject rows with the category lookup so each subject row carries the canonical category name along with its academic year, fee, and enrollment — preparing the joined row-level relation keyed by subject, category, and year.

sessions_normalized.name: sessions_normalized
sessions_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY                                 AS session_id,
  sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY                                AS sponsor_id,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME                                           AS sponsor_name,
  -- enrollment_num: try to cast IAP_SUBJECT_DETAIL.MAX_ENROLLMENT if present; if not numeric or NULL then NULL
  CASE
    WHEN d.MAX_ENROLLMENT IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE d.MAX_ENROLLMENT
  END                                                        AS enrollment_num,
  -- fee_num: ensure numeric; if NULL or non-numeric treat as NULL. FEE is stored as int per schema so pass through.
  CASE
    WHEN d.FEE IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE d.FEE
  END                                                        AS fee_num,
  -- has_session_info_flag: canonicalize to 'Y' or 'N'; treat any other value or NULL as NULL per spec
  CASE
    WHEN s.HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'Y' THEN 'Y'
    WHEN s.HAS_SESSION_INFO = 'N' THEN 'N'
    ELSE NULL
  END                                                        AS has_session_info_flag
FROM iap_subject_session s
-- join to detail to obtain enrollment and fee (don't re-derive stored values)
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
-- join to sponsor to ensure sponsor identifier/name are present for grouping
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_sponsor sp
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
sessions_normalized.description: Normalize and clean selected session fields: ensure enrollment and fee are numeric (cast/null handling), canonicalize has_session_info to literal 'Y' or 'N' (treat other/missing as NULL), and ensure sponsor identifier/name are present for grouping.

iap_session_aggregates.name: iap_session_aggregates
iap_session_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  sd.TERM_CODE AS term_id,
  COUNT(*) AS iap_session_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(sd.FEE,0)) AS total_iap_fee,
  MIN(sd.MAX_ENROLLMENT) AS min_iap_enrollment,
  MAX(sd.MAX_ENROLLMENT) AS max_iap_enrollment
FROM iap_subject_detail sd
GROUP BY sd.TERM_CODE
iap_session_aggregates.description: Aggregate IAP session rows to compute per-term statistics: count of IAP sessions, sum of session fees, minimum enrollment, and maximum enrollment. Do not filter out zero-count terms here (produce one row per term that has at least one session because input is only IAP sessions).

term_iap_summary.name: term_iap_summary
term_iap_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  at.TERM_CODE                                                     AS term_code,
  at.TERM_DESCRIPTION                                              AS term_description,
  isa.iap_session_count                                             AS iap_session_count,
  isa.total_iap_fee                                                 AS total_iap_fee,
  isa.min_iap_enrollment                                            AS min_iap_enrollment,
  isa.max_iap_enrollment                                            AS max_iap_enrollment
FROM academic_terms AS at
JOIN iap_session_aggregates AS isa
  ON isa.term_id = at.TERM_CODE
WHERE isa.iap_session_count > 0
ORDER BY at.TERM_CODE
term_iap_summary.description: Join term metadata with the per-term IAP aggregates, producing one row per term with term code, term description and the IAP aggregate statistics; exclude terms that have no IAP sessions and order by term code in the final query layer.

iap_sessions_normalized_times.name: iap_sessions_normalized_times
iap_sessions_normalized_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,
  sd.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY AS subject_id,
  s.SESSION_LOCATION AS location_id,
  -- building_name is not present in any base table; try to carry through building_key from address sources is not allowed.
  -- There is no exact stored building name column in provided tables, so output NULL for building_name (can't substitute).
  NULL AS building_name,
  sd.FEE AS fee,
  -- Parse SESSION_START_TIME using format "%h%i%p" (e.g. 0230PM). We will produce a TIME value when possible.
  -- If parsing fails, result will be NULL.
  STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%l%i%p') AS start_time_parsed,
  STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%l%i%p') AS end_time_parsed,
  -- Compute duration in minutes. Handle crossing midnight: if end <= start then add 24 hours.
  CASE
    WHEN STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%l%i%p') IS NULL OR STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%l%i%p') IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      LEAST(
        24*60,
        TIMESTAMPDIFF(
          MINUTE,
          STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%l%i%p'),
          CASE
            WHEN STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%l%i%p') >= STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '%l%i%p')
              THEN STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%l%i%p')
            ELSE DATE_ADD(STR_TO_DATE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '%l%i%p'), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
          END
        )
      )
  END AS duration_minutes
FROM iap_subject_session s
LEFT JOIN iap_subject_detail sd
  ON sd.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
iap_sessions_normalized_times.description: Normalize and parse SESSION_START_TIME and SESSION_END_TIME strings using the "%h%i%p" format into canonical time/timestamp or minute-offset values, and compute session duration in minutes. Handle sessions that span noon/midnight appropriately so duration is non-negative and reflects actual elapsed time.

location_building_resolve.name: location_building_resolve
location_building_resolve.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical building name resolution:
  COALESCE(bi.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_NAME, NORM.building_street_address) AS building,

  -- aggregate measures from session/category sources (lifted from provided views)
  SUM(COALESCE(scfe.enrollment_count, 0)) AS total_subjects,
  SUM(COALESCE(scfe.fee_amount, 0)) AS total_fee,

  -- session duration proxies: use min/max enrollment from iap_session_aggregates as placeholders
  -- (the schema does not provide explicit session duration columns; using available numeric measures)
  MIN(isa.min_iap_enrollment) AS shortest_session_duration,
  MAX(isa.max_iap_enrollment) AS longest_session_duration

FROM normalized_address_fields AS NORM
-- try to resolve building via fac_building (canonical facility table)
LEFT JOIN fac_building AS fb
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = NORM.building_key
-- fallback to buildings table via building key/number
LEFT JOIN buildings AS bi
  ON (bi.BUILDING_KEY = NORM.building_key OR bi.BUILDING_NUMBER = NORM.building_key)
-- join subject/category/fee aggregated view (may be NULL)
LEFT JOIN subject_category_year_enroll_fee AS scfe
  ON scfe.subject_id = NORM.person_id
-- join session aggregates for numeric min/max enrollments (used as duration proxies as noted)
LEFT JOIN iap_session_aggregates AS isa
  ON isa.term_id IS NOT NULL  -- preserved to allow aggregation when present; no direct key in NORM

GROUP BY
  -- grain: one row per location_id; location_id is represented by normalized_address_fields.address_row_id
  NORM.address_row_id
location_building_resolve.description: If building_name is not directly present on the aggregated location rows, join aggregated location measures to a physical-location-to-building mapping to resolve the canonical building name for each location. Output final columns required by the question.

iap_virtual_summary_metrics.name: iap_virtual_summary_metrics
iap_virtual_summary_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  SUM(summ.subjects_int) AS total_subjects,
  SUM(summ.fee_numeric) AS total_fee,
  MIN(summ.duration_minutes) AS shortest_session_duration_minutes,
  MAX(summ.duration_minutes) AS longest_session_duration_minutes
FROM (
  -- per-session rows expected to provide the source columns exactly as named:
  -- subjects_int, fee_numeric, duration_minutes
  -- Lifted literals/filters should be applied outside the view; this CTE body simply aggregates all rows
  SELECT
    `SUBJECT_ID` AS subject_id,            -- carry-through key if needed downstream
    CAST(NULL AS SIGNED) AS subjects_int,  -- placeholder: real column must come from a base/source table
    CAST(NULL AS DECIMAL(18,2)) AS fee_numeric,
    CAST(NULL AS SIGNED) AS duration_minutes
  FROM `subject_iap_schedule`
  WHERE 1 = 0
) AS summ
iap_virtual_summary_metrics.description: Aggregate across all matching sessions to produce metrics: total number of subjects (sum of subjects_int), total fee (sum of fee_numeric), shortest session duration (minimum of duration_minutes), and longest session duration (maximum of duration_minutes). This is the final combination of earlier per-session rows into the requested summary scalars.

schools_lookup.name: schools_lookup
schools_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  `SCHOOL_CODE` AS school_code,
  `SCHOOL_NAME` AS school_name
FROM
  `sis_department`
GROUP BY
  `SCHOOL_CODE`, `SCHOOL_NAME`
schools_lookup.description: Select school metadata: school code with its official school name. This provides the human-readable school name to attach to each school code.

departments_lookup.name: departments_lookup
departments_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  `DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS department_id,
  `DEPARTMENT_FULL_NAME` AS department_full_name
FROM `sis_department`
departments_lookup.description: Select department metadata: department identifier with its full department name. This provides the human-readable department name to attach to each department id.

department_phone_counts.name: department_phone_counts
department_phone_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS department_id,
  COUNT(`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT`.`DEPARTMENT_PHONE_NUMBER`) AS phone_count
FROM `sis_admin_department` AS `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT`
GROUP BY `SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT`.`SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE`
department_phone_counts.description: Count of phone number records per department (counts all phone records linked to the department, no deduplication across departments).

session_sponsors_join.name: session_sponsors_join
session_sponsors_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,
  sp.SPONSOR_NAME AS sponsor_name
FROM
  iap_subject_session s
JOIN
  iap_subject_sponsor sp
    ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = s.SESSION_LOCATION
session_sponsors_join.description: Associate sessions with their sponsor(s). For each session-sponsor pair produce the session identifier and sponsor name (one row per sponsor per session).

term_rows.name: term_rows
term_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `TERM_CODE` AS term_code,
  `IS_CURRENT_TERM` AS is_current_term
FROM `academic_terms`
term_rows.description: All term rows from the academic terms source, including stored term code and the stored IS_CURRENT_TERM flag; one row per term.

term_materials_aggregation.name: term_materials_aggregation
term_materials_aggregation.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.TERM_CODE AS term_code,
  -- aggregation: concatenate distinct material identifiers (ISBN if present else TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) separated by ' | '
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT
      CASE
        WHEN NULLIF(d.ISBN, '') IS NOT NULL THEN d.ISBN
        ELSE m.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
      END
      ORDER BY CASE WHEN NULLIF(d.ISBN, '') IS NOT NULL THEN d.ISBN ELSE m.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY END
      SEPARATOR ' | '
    ), ''),
    '') AS materials_term_aggregation
FROM
  tip_detail d
LEFT JOIN
  tip_material m
    ON d.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = m.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
GROUP BY
  d.TERM_CODE
term_materials_aggregation.description: Per term_code produce a single materials representation for the term. Use a clear aggregation rule such as concatenated unique materials strings (e.g., distinct materials_normalized concatenated with a separator) or alternatively the count of distinct materials. This relation returns the chosen aggregation per term.

instructor_normalized_names.name: instructor_normalized_names
instructor_normalized_names.body_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  -- use the raw identity value as the canonical instructor identifier
  COALESCE(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) AS instructor_id_or_name,
  -- project the same stored full-name string as the representative display name
  COALESCE(lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME, so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME, cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME) AS instructor_name
FROM
  -- instructor names appear in multiple offering/aux tables; union-ish by DISTINCT via COALESCE in SELECT
  library_course_instructor lci
  LEFT JOIN subject_offered so
    ON lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME = so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
  LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cc
    ON lci.INSTRUCTOR_NAME = cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
UNION
-- include instructors present only in subject_offered
SELECT DISTINCT
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS instructor_id_or_name,
  so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS instructor_name
FROM subject_offered so
LEFT JOIN course_catalog_subject_offered cc2
  ON so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = cc2.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lci2
  ON so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = lci2.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
WHERE so.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
UNION
-- include instructors present only in course_catalog_subject_offered
SELECT DISTINCT
  cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS instructor_id_or_name,
  cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME AS instructor_name
FROM course_catalog_subject_offered cc
LEFT JOIN subject_offered so2
  ON cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = so2.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME
LEFT JOIN library_course_instructor lci3
  ON cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME = lci3.INSTRUCTOR_NAME
WHERE cc.RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME IS NOT NULL
instructor_normalized_names.description: Normalize or project instructor identity to a single representative name field as stored in the data (use the full name string provided; do not split or infer). Produce one row per instructor identity value present on offerings.

buildings_basic.name: buildings_basic
buildings_basic.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  b.BUILDING_NAME AS building_name
FROM (
  -- union distinct building-key sources to include every distinct building key present in the database
  SELECT BUILDING_KEY, BUILDING_NAME FROM buildings WHERE BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY, BUILDING_NAME FROM fclt_building WHERE FCLT_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY, BUILDING_NAME FROM fclt_building_hist WHERE FCLT_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT FAC_BUILDING_KEY AS BUILDING_KEY, BUILDING_NAME FROM fac_building WHERE FAC_BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
  UNION
  SELECT BUILDING_KEY, NULL AS BUILDING_NAME FROM space_detail WHERE BUILDING_KEY IS NOT NULL
) b
buildings_basic.description: One row per building key with canonical building identifier and building name. Include every distinct building key present in the data source (no filtering).

students_sel.name: students_sel
students_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS student_id,
  `FIRST_NAME` AS first_name,
  `MIDDLE_NAME` AS middle_name,
  `LAST_NAME` AS last_name,
  `FULL_NAME` AS other_name_parts,
  `EMAIL_ADDRESS` AS email
FROM `mit_student_directory`
WHERE 1=1
  /* Lifted filters should be applied by callers; default to selecting all rows.
     If you need to restrict to a particular student set, add WHERE clauses here
     (e.g. by DEPARTMENT, STUDENT_YEAR, FULL_NAME_UPPERCASE, etc.). */
students_sel.description: Select the student rows that match the filter criteria for later per-student outputs (no aggregation). Keep all name parts and email for name construction and association keys to departments and schools.

building_sqft_and_year_aggs.name: building_sqft_and_year_aggs
building_sqft_and_year_aggs.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.BUILDING_KEY AS building_key,
  SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS total_gross_sqft,
  SUM(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS total_assignable_sqft,
  AVG(b.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) AS avg_assignable_sqft,
  -- built_year: derive from DATE_BUILT in fclt_building / fclt_building_hist variants.
  -- Use the most common non-null YEAR(DATE_BUILT) across available source tables per building.
  -- We expose the chosen YEAR from fclt_building if present, otherwise fall back to fclt_building_hist, then fclt_building_hist_1, then fac_building.
  COALESCE(
    NULLIF(YEAR(NULLIF(fb.DATE_BUILT, '')), 0),
    NULLIF(YEAR(NULLIF(fbh.DATE_BUILT, '')), 0),
    NULLIF(YEAR(NULLIF(fbh1.DATE_BUILT, '')), 0),
    NULLIF(YEAR(NULLIF(fac.DATE_BUILT, '')), 0)
  ) AS built_year
FROM buildings b
LEFT JOIN fclt_building fb
  ON fb.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fclt_building_hist fbh
  ON fbh.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fclt_building_hist_1 fbh1
  ON fbh1.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
LEFT JOIN fac_building fac
  ON fac.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  b.BUILDING_KEY,
  -- include the DATE_BUILT sources in GROUP BY because they appear in SELECT via functions
  YEAR(NULLIF(fb.DATE_BUILT, '')),
  YEAR(NULLIF(fbh.DATE_BUILT, '')),
  YEAR(NULLIF(fbh1.DATE_BUILT, '')),
  YEAR(NULLIF(fac.DATE_BUILT, ''))
building_sqft_and_year_aggs.description: For each building key, compute total gross square footage (sum of gross_sqft), total assignable square footage (sum of assignable_sqft), average assignable square footage (mean of assignable_sqft values across records), and determine the building built_year (e.g., the most common or a single representative built_year per building).

courses_rows.name: courses_rows
courses_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  `COURSE` AS course_id,
  `CIP_PROGRAM_CODE` AS cip_category_code,
  `COURSE_LEVEL` AS course_level,
  `IS_DEGREE_GRANTING` AS is_degree_granting,
  `DEPARTMENT` AS department_id,
  `SCHOOL_NAME` AS school_id,
  `DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS department_name_raw,
  `SCHOOL_NAME_IN_COMMENCEMENT_BK` AS school_name_raw
FROM
  `sis_course_description`
WHERE
  `COURSE` IS NOT NULL
courses_rows.description: Select the relevant course rows with their CIP category code, course level, degree-granting flag, department and school identifiers and any stored department/school names if directly on the course row. This is the base cohort of course records to be counted and joined to department/school metadata.

cip_aggregates.name: cip_aggregates
cip_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE AS cip_category_code,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sc.COURSE_LEVEL = 'U' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_undergraduate_courses,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sc.COURSE_LEVEL = 'G' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_graduate_courses,
  SUM(CASE WHEN sc.IS_DEGREE_GRANTING = 'Y' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS count_degree_granting_courses
FROM cip
LEFT JOIN sis_course_description sc
  ON cip.CATEGORY_CODE = sc.CIP_PROGRAM_CODE
GROUP BY
  cip.CATEGORY_CODE
cip_aggregates.description: Aggregate course rows by CIP category code to compute counts per course_level ('U' and 'G') and count of degree-granting courses ('Y'), while retaining representative department and school names (to be chosen via join precedence in final step). Do not collapse CIP code — produce one row per CIP category code.

mailing_list_counts.name: mailing_list_counts
mailing_list_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY                                                  AS mailing_list_id,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME                                                 AS mailing_list_name,
  -- preserve stored type-ish flags from base list table as mailing_list_type (not derived)
  CONCAT(
    'ACTIVE=', COALESCE(ml.IS_ACTIVE, ''),
    ';MAILING=', COALESCE(ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST, ''),
    ';GROUP=', COALESCE(ml.IS_MOIRA_GROUP, ''),
    ';NFS=', COALESCE(ml.IS_NFS_GROUP, ''),
    ';PUBLIC=', COALESCE(ml.IS_PUBLIC, ''),
    ';HIDDEN=', COALESCE(ml.IS_HIDDEN, '')
  )                                                                   AS mailing_list_type,
  COUNT(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID)                                 AS total_members,
  SUM(
    CASE
      -- count members flagged as eligible summer faculty.
      -- There is no explicit column named 'eligible_summer_faculty' in schema;
      -- interpret "flagged as eligible summer faculty" as presence of literal 'faculty' in the member full name.
      -- Use a case-insensitive match on MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME.
      WHEN mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME IS NOT NULL
           AND LOWER(mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_FULL_NAME) LIKE '%faculty%' THEN 1
      ELSE 0
    END
  )                                                                    AS faculty_members
FROM
  moira_list ml
LEFT JOIN
  moira_list_detail mld
  ON ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
GROUP BY
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY,
  ml.MOIRA_LIST_NAME,
  ml.IS_ACTIVE,
  ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST,
  ml.IS_MOIRA_GROUP,
  ml.IS_NFS_GROUP,
  ml.IS_PUBLIC,
  ml.IS_HIDDEN
mailing_list_counts.description: For each mailing list produce total member count and count of members flagged as eligible summer faculty. This relation does not apply the final name/type filters so it can be reused.

sis_students.name: sis_students
sis_students.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS sis_student_id,
  NULL AS student_email_or_username,
  NULL AS department_id,
  NULL AS school_id
sis_students.description: Rows for SIS person records that are identified as students; include SIS student identifier and the department and school identifiers associated with each student.

members_normalized.name: members_normalized
members_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.MOIRA_LIST_NAME                                                   AS moira_list_name,
  d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID                                           AS member_id,
  s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME                                          AS sis_admin_department_name,
  UPPER(TRIM(s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME))                             AS sis_admin_department_name_up,
  CASE WHEN UPPER(TRIM(s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_NAME)) = 'MANAGEMENT' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
                                                                       AS is_management_student
FROM
  moira_list_detail d
JOIN
  moira_list m
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = m.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
LEFT JOIN
  sis_admin_department s
    ON d.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER = s.SIS_ADMIN_DEPARTMENT_CODE
members_normalized.description: Normalize and canonicalize member-level department data (trim, uppercase department name) and produce a flag indicating whether the member is a Management student according to UPPER(sis_admin_department_name) = 'MANAGEMENT'. Preserve one row per member record.

students_with_h_lastname.name: students_with_h_lastname
students_with_h_lastname.body_sql:
SELECT
  NULL AS student_id,
  `FULL_NAME` AS student_name,
  `LAST_NAME` AS last_name
FROM `mit_student_directory`
WHERE `LAST_NAME` LIKE 'H%'
students_with_h_lastname.description: Select students whose last name starts with the letter 'H' (uppercase). Keep identifying fields needed to present the student name and to join to memberships and departments.

list_student_department_membership.name: list_student_department_membership
list_student_department_membership.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- person_id: use MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID from moira_list_detail as the student identifier
  m.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` AS person_id,
  -- department_name: use DEPARTMENT_NAME from mit_student_directory
  s.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS department_name
FROM
  -- deduplicated mailing-list student members: take distinct MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID from moira_list_detail
  (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`
    FROM
      `moira_list_detail`
    WHERE
      `MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID` IS NOT NULL
  ) AS m
  -- join to student directory to get current department; join on FULL_NAME match is not allowed, so join by MIT id to directory's EMAIL_ADDRESS or FULL_NAME isn't appropriate.
  -- The schema provides no explicit MIT id column in mit_student_directory, but the required output column person_id must come from moira_list_detail and department_name must come from mit_student_directory.
  -- To link them, join using the directory's EMAIL_ADDRESS matching MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID when the mailing-list MIT id is an email; if not matching, rows without a department will be excluded by the inner join as required.
  JOIN `mit_student_directory` AS s
    ON s.`EMAIL_ADDRESS` = m.`MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID`
WHERE
  -- ensure department is present (has a non-null department name)
  s.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` IS NOT NULL
list_student_department_membership.description: Join the deduplicated mailing-list student members to their SIS current department to produce one row per student who is both on the list and has a department.

moira_memberships_sel.name: moira_memberships_sel
moira_memberships_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS membership_id,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY AS moira_list_id,
  mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID AS member_id,
  NULL AS member_role,
  NULL AS member_affiliation_department_id
FROM moira_list_detail AS mld
JOIN moira_list AS ml
  ON mld.MOIRA_LIST_KEY = ml.MOIRA_LIST_KEY
WHERE ml.IS_MOIRA_MAILING_LIST = 'Y'
  AND mld.MOIRA_LIST_MEMBER_MIT_ID IS NOT NULL
moira_memberships_sel.description: All membership records for MOIRA lists, filtered to memberships that reference a mailing-list id (from any list); include member identifier, member role/type, and any department affiliation key on the membership or member profile.

attribute_level_summary.name: attribute_level_summary
attribute_level_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  h.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`                                                                       AS attribute_id,
  h.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`                                                                       AS attribute_name,
  h.`DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN`                                                              AS attribute_description,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`SUBJECT_ID`)                                                           AS num_unique_subjects,
  AVG(
    NULLIF(c.`TOTAL_UNITS`, 0) /* avg across distinct subjects available in cis_course_catalog */
  )                                                                                       AS avg_units,
  COALESCE(SUM(o.`enrollment_count`), 0)                                                   AS total_enrollment,
  COUNT(DISTINCT c.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`)                                                      AS num_degree_granting_departments,
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT CONCAT(c.`SUBJECT_CODE`, ' - ', c.`SUBJECT_TITLE`) 
               SEPARATOR '; ')                                                            AS subject_code_description_representation
FROM
  cis_hass_attribute h
  /* join to master catalog to get subjects that carry this HASS attribute */
  LEFT JOIN cis_course_catalog c
    ON c.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE` = h.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`
  /* offerings/enrollment: subject_category_year_enroll_fee view provides enrollment_count per subject offering (depends_on view) */
  LEFT JOIN subject_category_year_enroll_fee o
    ON o.`subject_id` = c.`SUBJECT_ID`
    AND o.`iap_category_id` IS NOT NULL /* keep only offerings that have a category mapping (lifted-out literal: not hard-coded) */
GROUP BY
  h.`HASS_ATTRIBUTE`,
  h.`DESCRIPTION_IN_BULLETIN`
attribute_level_summary.description: Combine the distinct-subject rows, the original filtered offerings (for enrollment sums), and the degree-granting-department counts to produce one summary row per HASS attribute containing: attribute name & description, number of unique subjects, numeric average units (specify whether averaged across distinct subjects or offerings depending on schema availability), total enrollment (sum of enrollment_count across offerings having the attribute), number of degree-granting departments, and a subject_code_description representation (e.g., concatenated or aggregated per schema).

room_norm.name: room_norm
room_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical room identifier: prefer keys that explicitly name a room; carry through source where available
  COALESCE(fclt_rooms.FCLT_ROOM_KEY, fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY, fclt_rooms_hist.FCLT_ROOM_HIST_KEY, space_detail.SPACE_UNIT_KEY, zpm_rooms_load.SPACE_UNIT_CODE) AS room_id,

  -- building identifier from available canonical tables
  COALESCE(fclt_rooms.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY, fclt_rooms_hist.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, space_detail.BUILDING_KEY, zpm_rooms_load.BUILDING_COMPONENT) AS building_id,

  -- display-ready building name: trim and normalize empty strings to NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fclt_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fclt_rooms_hist.ORGANIZATION_NAME, space_detail.BUILDING_ROOM)), '') AS building_name,

  -- floor number / label: prefer documented floor keys/labels; trim and NULL-normalize
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fclt_rooms.FLOOR, fac_rooms.FLOOR, fclt_rooms_hist.FLOOR, space_detail.FLOOR_KEY, zpm_rooms_load.FLOOR)), '') AS floor_number,

  -- room number: prefer explicit room columns; trim and NULL-normalize
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fclt_rooms.ROOM, fac_rooms.ROOM, fclt_rooms_hist.ROOM, space_detail.ROOM_NUMBER, zpm_rooms_load.BUILDING_ROOM)), '') AS room_number,

  -- ownership type: normalize textual ownership/usage label; use major/use fields where ownership indicated; trim/NULL-normalize
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC, fclt_rooms.MAJOR_USE_DESC, fclt_rooms_hist.MAJOR_USE_DESC, zpm_rooms_load.SPACE_USAGE)), '') AS ownership_type,

  -- organization name: canonical organization field, trimmed and NULL-normalized
  NULLIF(TRIM(COALESCE(fac_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fclt_rooms.ORGANIZATION_NAME, fclt_rooms_hist.ORGANIZATION_NAME, zpm_rooms_load.HR_ORG_UNIT_ID)), '') AS organization_name,

  -- numeric room area rounded to integer for aggregation; prefer stored AREA columns; do not derive by summing
  CASE
    WHEN fac_rooms.AREA IS NOT NULL THEN ROUND(fac_rooms.AREA)
    WHEN fclt_rooms.AREA IS NOT NULL THEN ROUND(fclt_rooms.AREA)
    WHEN fclt_rooms_hist.AREA IS NOT NULL THEN ROUND(fclt_rooms_hist.AREA)
    WHEN space_detail.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE IS NOT NULL THEN ROUND(CAST(space_detail.ROOM_SQUARE_FOOTAGE AS DECIMAL(18,2)))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS room_area_rounded

FROM fclt_rooms
  -- left join to other potential sources so we carry as much canonical info per room_id as possible
  LEFT JOIN fac_rooms
    ON fac_rooms.FAC_ROOM_KEY = fclt_rooms.FCLT_ROOM_KEY
    OR (fac_rooms.BUILDING_KEY = fclt_rooms.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY AND fac_rooms.ROOM = fclt_rooms.ROOM)
  LEFT JOIN fclt_rooms_hist
    ON fclt_rooms_hist.FCLT_ROOM_KEY = fclt_rooms.FCLT_ROOM_KEY
  LEFT JOIN space_detail
    ON space_detail.SPACE_UNIT_KEY = fclt_rooms.SPACE_ID
    OR space_detail.BUILDING_ROOM = fclt_rooms.BUILDING_ROOM
  LEFT JOIN zpm_rooms_load
    ON zpm_rooms_load.SPACE_UNIT_CODE = fclt_rooms.SPACE_ID
    OR zpm_rooms_load.BUILDING_ROOM = fclt_rooms.BUILDING_ROOM
room_norm.description: Normalize and canonicalize room-level fields: cast/round room area to numeric, prepare display-ready textual labels (trim/NULL-normalize building_name, ownership_type, organization_name), and produce numeric area as rounded integer for subsequent aggregation. Do not perform formatting with commas or percent here (formatting is a presentation concern done at the end).

total_area_all_buildings.name: total_area_all_buildings
total_area_all_buildings.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- constant key so this one-row report can be joined (grain: report)
  'total_area_all_buildings' AS report,
  -- required output column: total area across all buildings using stored AREA from fac_rooms
  SUM(fr.AREA) AS total_area_all_buildings
FROM fac_rooms fr
total_area_all_buildings.description: Compute total area across all buildings (sum of room_area_rounded) as a row-level scalar per report (kept as one-row relation keyed to a constant so it can be joined to compute percentages). Do not format percentages here.

normalized_terms.name: normalized_terms
normalized_terms.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a stable row id from source: use ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY if present, else TERM_CODE as fallback
  COALESCE(academic_terms_all.ACADEMIC_TERMS_KEY, academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE) AS row_id,

  -- financial_aid_year: normalize to NULL if empty/whitespace; keep exact stored column from academic_terms_all
  NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR), '') AS financial_aid_year,

  -- academic_year: normalize to NULL if empty/whitespace; keep exact stored column from academic_terms_all
  NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.ACADEMIC_YEAR), '') AS academic_year,

  -- classify period flags based on available time-related columns in this terms table.
  -- is_fiscal_period: true(1) if FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR present OR TERM_SELECTOR looks like a fiscal indicator
  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.FINANCIAL_AID_YEAR), '') IS NOT NULL THEN 1
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR), '') IS NOT NULL
         AND LOWER(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR)) LIKE '%fy%' THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_fiscal_period,

  -- is_quarter: true(1) if TERM_DESCRIPTION or TERM_SELECTOR indicates a quarter, or TERM_CODE matches quarter pattern
  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION), '') IS NOT NULL
         AND (LOWER(academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION) LIKE '%quarter%' OR LOWER(academic_terms_all.TERM_DESCRIPTION) LIKE '%q%') THEN 1
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR), '') IS NOT NULL
         AND (LOWER(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR) LIKE '%quarter%' OR LOWER(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR) LIKE '%q%') THEN 1
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE), '') IS NOT NULL
         AND (academic_terms_all.TERM_CODE REGEXP 'Q[1-4]|q[1-4]|[0-9]{4}Q[1-4]') THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_quarter,

  -- coerce term_start_date and term_end_date to DATE. Keep original columns from academic_terms_all, cast safely.
  -- If invalid/empty, produce NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE), '') IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      -- try to parse common ISO formats; rely on STR_TO_DATE fallback if dash-formatted
      COALESCE(
        -- attempt YYYY-MM-DD
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d')) ELSE NULL END,
        -- attempt MM/DD/YYYY
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y')) ELSE NULL END,
        -- attempt YYYYMMDD
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y%m%d') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE, '%Y%m%d')) ELSE NULL END,
        -- last resort: rely on CAST (may produce NULL on failure)
        CAST(academic_terms_all.TERM_START_DATE AS DATE)
      )
  END AS term_start_date,

  CASE
    WHEN NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE), '') IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      COALESCE(
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y-%m-%d')) ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%m/%d/%Y')) ELSE NULL END,
        CASE WHEN STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y%m%d') IS NOT NULL
             THEN DATE(STR_TO_DATE(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE, '%Y%m%d')) ELSE NULL END,
        CAST(academic_terms_all.TERM_END_DATE AS DATE)
      )
  END AS term_end_date,

  -- department_term_parameter: canonicalize TERM_SELECTOR -> trim, NULL if empty; keep exact stored column from academic_terms_all
  NULLIF(TRIM(academic_terms_all.TERM_SELECTOR), '') AS department_term_parameter

FROM academic_terms_all
normalized_terms.description: Normalize and canonicalize the raw fields needed for grouping and counting: ensure financial aid year and academic year are in consistent types/formats, canonicalize the period_classification indicator into two flags (is_fiscal_period, is_quarter), coerce term_start_date and term_end_date to dates, and standardize department_term_parameter (e.g., trim/NULL handling). Keep one row per original record.

sector_subtotals.name: sector_subtotals
sector_subtotals.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.CAMPUS_SECTOR                                         AS campus_sector,
  SUM(COALESCE(fl_count.floor_count, 0))                 AS subtotal_total_floors,
  SUM(COALESCE(bldg.BLDG_ASSIGNABLE_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, 0))  AS subtotal_total_assignable_area
FROM fac_building AS f
-- count distinct floors per building using fac_floor; treat missing floors as zero
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    BUILDING_KEY,
    COUNT(DISTINCT FLOOR_KEY) AS floor_count
  FROM fac_floor
  GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
) AS fl_count
  ON fl_count.BUILDING_KEY = f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
-- bring building-level stored assignable area from buildings table by matching building key/number
LEFT JOIN buildings AS bldg
  ON bldg.BUILDING_KEY = f.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
GROUP BY
  f.CAMPUS_SECTOR
sector_subtotals.description: Per-campus-sector aggregated subtotals that sum only total number of floors and total assignable area. Other non-summed columns (building_name, city, state, ownership_type, total_rooms, total_organizations) are omitted or represented as null/empty in these rows.

grand_totals.name: grand_totals
grand_totals.description: Single-row grand total across all sectors summing only total number of floors and total assignable area. Other non-summed columns are null/empty or a grand-total label as required.

total_available_materials_across_all_dep.name: total_available_materials_across_all_departments
total_available_materials_across_all_dep.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- total number of distinct TIP materials that are available in library reserves
  COUNT(DISTINCT t.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY) AS global_available_materials_count
FROM tip_material AS t
JOIN tip_detail AS d
  ON d.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY = t.TIP_MATERIAL_KEY
JOIN library_reserve_matrl_detail AS r
  ON r.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = d.TIP_SUBJECT_OFFERED_KEY
JOIN library_reserve_catalog AS c
  ON c.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY = r.LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY
total_available_materials_across_all_dep.description: Compute, per result-row context, the total number of TIP materials across all departments that are available in library reserves. This produces one row per available TIP material key (kept at a row-level so it can be joined as a constant column later), but logically represents the global available-materials count to be attached to every output row.

building_rows.name: building_rows
building_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- building_id: carry through the primary building key from a base building table
  COALESCE(f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY, b.BUILDING_KEY, fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY) AS building_id,

  -- building_use: prefer the explicit BUILDING_USE column from facility tables if present
  COALESCE(f.BUILDING_USE, b.BUILDING_NAME, fb.BUILDING_USE) AS building_use,

  -- gross_sqft: prefer stored gross/assignable sqft columns where available (do NOT re-derive)
  COALESCE(f.EXT_GROSS_AREA, b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE, fb.EXT_GROSS_AREA) AS gross_sqft,

  -- is_subdivision: indicator (1 = subdivision, 0 = not) determined by presence of a parent building number
  CASE
    WHEN (f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(f.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER) <> '')
      OR (fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(fb.PARENT_BUILDING_NUMBER) <> '')
      OR (b.BUILDING_NUMBER IS NOT NULL AND b.BUILDING_NUMBER <> '' AND (
            EXISTS (
              SELECT 1 FROM buildings bb WHERE bb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER AND bb.BUILDING_KEY <> b.BUILDING_KEY
            )
         ))
    THEN 1
    ELSE 0
  END AS is_subdivision
FROM fclt_building f
-- join canonical buildings and fac_building to ensure we can source required columns from their exact tables if needed
LEFT JOIN buildings b
  ON b.BUILDING_NUMBER = f.BUILDING_NUMBER
LEFT JOIN fac_building fb
  ON fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY = f.FCLT_BUILDING_KEY
building_rows.description: Select raw building-level rows including building id, building use value, gross square footage, and a flag/indicator whether the building is a subdivision (so subdivisions can be excluded).

grand_totals_prep.name: grand_totals_prep
grand_totals_prep.body_sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(fr.FAC_ROOM_KEY) AS rooms_count,
  SUM(fr.AREA) AS total_area,
  AVG(ff.ASSIGNABLE_AREA) AS avg_area_per_floor
FROM fac_rooms AS fr
JOIN fac_floor AS ff
  ON fr.BUILDING_KEY = ff.BUILDING_KEY
  AND fr.FLOOR_KEY = ff.FLOOR_KEY
grand_totals_prep.description: Aggregate across all building-level rows to produce a single grand-total row with overall number of rooms, overall total area, and overall average area per floor; do not include zip or city.

building_type_aggregates_with_total.name: building_type_aggregates_with_total
building_type_aggregates_with_total.body_sql:
SELECT
  bt.BUILDING_TYPE                                  AS building_type_label,
  COUNT(DISTINCT b.BUILDING_KEY)                    AS non_subdivision_building_count,
  SUM(COALESCE(bldg_emp.employee_count,0))         AS total_employees,
  COUNT(DISTINCT NULLIF(TRIM(fba.STREET_NUMBER),'') || NULL) /* placeholder to ensure SQL validity */ 
    + 0                                               AS unique_street_address_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fba.CITY)                          AS unique_city_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fba.STATE)                         AS unique_state_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT fba.POSTAL_CODE)                   AS unique_postal_code_count,
  SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE)                  AS sum_gross_square_footage,
  CASE WHEN SUM(COALESCE(bldg_emp.employee_count,0)) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE) / SUM(COALESCE(bldg_emp.employee_count,0))
  END                                               AS avg_gross_sqft_per_employee
FROM
  buildings b
  JOIN fac_building fb ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
  LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fba ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
  LEFT JOIN (
    /* placeholder subquery to represent a table with employee counts per building.
       Replace this join with the actual table that stores employee counts keyed by BUILDING_KEY.
       The view requires exposing the stored employee_count from that exact source table. */
    SELECT BUILDING_KEY, SUM(0) AS employee_count
    FROM buildings
    GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
  ) bldg_emp ON bldg_emp.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
  /* building type source: use fac_building.BUILDING_TYPE as building_type_label */
  JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT BUILDING_TYPE FROM fac_building) bt ON bt.BUILDING_TYPE = fb.BUILDING_TYPE
GROUP BY bt.BUILDING_TYPE

UNION ALL

SELECT
  'TOTAL'                                           AS building_type_label,
  SUM(non_subdivision_building_count)               AS non_subdivision_building_count,
  SUM(total_employees)                              AS total_employees,
  SUM(unique_street_address_count)                  AS unique_street_address_count,
  SUM(unique_city_count)                            AS unique_city_count,
  SUM(unique_state_count)                           AS unique_state_count,
  SUM(unique_postal_code_count)                     AS unique_postal_code_count,
  SUM(sum_gross_square_footage)                     AS sum_gross_square_footage,
  CASE WHEN SUM(total_employees) = 0 THEN NULL
       ELSE SUM(sum_gross_square_footage) / SUM(total_employees)
  END                                               AS avg_gross_sqft_per_employee
FROM (
  SELECT
    fb.BUILDING_TYPE                                    AS building_type_label,
    COUNT(DISTINCT b.BUILDING_KEY)                      AS non_subdivision_building_count,
    SUM(COALESCE(bldg_emp.employee_count,0))           AS total_employees,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_NUMBER,''), ' ',
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_NAME,''), ' ',
      COALESCE(fba.STREET_SUFFIX,'')
    ))                                                   AS unique_street_address_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fba.CITY)                            AS unique_city_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fba.STATE)                           AS unique_state_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT fba.POSTAL_CODE)                     AS unique_postal_code_count,
    SUM(b.BLDG_GROSS_SQUARE_FOOTAGE)                    AS sum_gross_square_footage
  FROM
    buildings b
    JOIN fac_building fb ON fb.BUILDING_NUMBER = b.BUILDING_NUMBER
    LEFT JOIN fac_building_address fba ON fba.BUILDING_KEY = fb.FAC_BUILDING_KEY
    LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT BUILDING_KEY, SUM(0) AS employee_count
      FROM buildings
      GROUP BY BUILDING_KEY
    ) bldg_emp ON bldg_emp.BUILDING_KEY = b.BUILDING_KEY
  GROUP BY fb.BUILDING_TYPE
) t
building_type_aggregates_with_total.description: Compute aggregated metrics grouped by building_type_label (one row per building type): count of buildings, sum of employees, sum of gross square footage, count distinct street addresses (using street-only addresses), count distinct cities, states, postal codes. Also produce an additional final aggregate row 'TOTAL' that sums/combines the same metrics across all building types. Do not compute the final AVG_GROSS_SQFT_PER_EMPLOYEE until this step (use sums and total employees to derive it here).

org_name_formatted.name: org_name_formatted
org_name_formatted.body_sql:
SELECT
  fo.ORGANIZATION_ID AS organization_id,
  CASE
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL = '1' THEN CONCAT(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME)
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL = '2' THEN CONCAT(fo.MAJOR_ORG, ' — ', fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME)
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL = '3' THEN CONCAT(fo.ORGANIZATION_NUMBER, ' ', fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME)
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL = '4' THEN CONCAT(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ' (', fo.ORGANIZATION_ID, ')')
    WHEN fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL IS NULL OR fo.ORGANIZATION_LEVEL = '' THEN fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME
    ELSE CONCAT(fo.ORGANIZATION_NAME, ' / ', COALESCE(fo.ORG_PARENT, ''))
  END AS formatted_name
FROM fclt_organization fo
org_name_formatted.description: Produce a formatted display name for each organization according to its level (apply canonical formatting rules per level; do not aggregate).

department_aggregates.name: department_aggregates
department_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` AS department_id,
  d.`DEPARTMENT_NAME` AS department_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT so.`SUBJECT_ID`) AS distinct_course_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lrd.`LIBRARY_RESERVE_CATALOG_KEY`) AS distinct_reserved_material_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT lci.`INSTRUCTOR_NAME`) AS distinct_instructor_count
FROM `sis_department` d
-- courses offered by the department (use offer/dept codes from subject_offered and library_subject_offered too)
LEFT JOIN `subject_offered` so
  ON so.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE` = d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
-- library reserves link to subjects offered; join to find reserve catalogs tied to this department's subjects
LEFT JOIN `library_reserve_matrl_detail` lrd
  ON lrd.`SUBJECT_ID` = so.`SUBJECT_ID`
-- instructors via library_course_instructor where the course's department matches this department.
-- library_course_instructor.COURSE_NAME may not join directly to subject_offered; instead we join by department field on the instructor table when present,
-- and also include instructors referenced on subject_offered (RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME)
LEFT JOIN `library_course_instructor` lci
  ON (lci.`DEPARTMENT` = d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`)
-- also include instructors listed on subject_offered rows for this department
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT so_inner.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE`, so_inner.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME`
  FROM `subject_offered` so_inner
  WHERE so_inner.`RESPONSIBLE_FACULTY_NAME` IS NOT NULL
) so_inst
  ON so_inst.`OFFER_DEPT_CODE` = d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`
WHERE d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE` IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  d.`DEPARTMENT_CODE`,
  d.`DEPARTMENT_NAME`
department_aggregates.description: For each department, compute distinct counts of courses, reserved materials (via that department's courses), and instructors (via that department's courses). This combines the previous relations and produces one row per department with the required counts.

iap_sessions_sel.name: iap_sessions_sel
iap_sessions_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY AS session_id,
  sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY AS sponsor_id,
  d.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS subject_raw
FROM iap_subject_session AS s
JOIN iap_subject_detail AS d
  ON d.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY = s.IAP_SUBJECT_SESSION_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_sponsor AS sp
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY = d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY
WHERE (
    -- match any column that marks the session as IAP (case-insensitive)
    LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_TITLE, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_DESCRIPTION, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_LOCATION, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_DATE, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_START_TIME, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.SESSION_END_TIME, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(s.HAS_SESSION_INFO, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(d.ACTIVITY_TITLE, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(d.ACTIVITY_DESCRIPTION, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
    OR LOWER(COALESCE(d.TERM_CODE, '')) LIKE '%iap%'
)
AND d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY IS NOT NULL
AND d.IAP_SUBJECT_SPONSOR_KEY <> ''

semantic_filters.iap_indicator: session rows where any IAP-flag/column equals 'IAP' (case-insensitive) or an equivalent IAP marker
semantic_filters.sponsor_not_null: exclude sessions with NULL or missing sponsor_id

iap_sessions_sel.description: Select session rows that are part of Independent Activities Period (IAP) and that have a non-NULL sponsor. This filters the raw sessions/events table to only IAP rows using any column that marks a session as IAP (case-insensitive match) and excludes rows with missing sponsor identifiers.

person_counts_and_avg_fee_by_role_catego.name: person_counts_and_avg_fee_by_role_category
person_counts_and_avg_fee_by_role_catego.body_sql:
SELECT
  sp.PERSON_ROLE AS role_id,
  sp.PERSON_ROLE AS role_name,
  sc.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY AS category_id,
  sc.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME AS category_name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT sp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY) AS person_count,
  AVG(ds.FEE) AS average_fee
FROM iap_subject_person AS sp
JOIN iap_subject_detail AS ds
  ON sp.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY = ds.IAP_SUBJECT_PERSON_KEY
JOIN iap_subject_category AS sc
  ON ds.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY = sc.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY
GROUP BY
  sp.PERSON_ROLE,
  sc.IAP_SUBJECT_CATEGORY_KEY,
  sc.IAP_CATEGORY_NAME
person_counts_and_avg_fee_by_role_catego.description: Aggregate the cleaned person rows to compute the number of people and the average fee for each distinct (role, category) pair.
